clue.text: Most evil since being boxed by finest

indicators.note: being boxed by means the word for since sits enclosed within the word for finest

parts.note: finest means best
as can mean since, as in 'as it was raining'

explanation.surface: A boxer's corner man explains why the villain is the worst: he is facing the best fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means morally low or wicked, so its superlative is the wickedest of all.

clue.text: Head of buddleia emerges producing flowers

indicators.note: Head of tells us to take the first letter of buddleia

parts.note: looms means comes into view or emerges

explanation.surface: A buddleia bush puts out its first flower spike in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blooms are flowers, especially those of a decorative plant in full blossom.

clue.text: Front line deviously reshaped round middle of war

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the middle letter of war
deviously means by a winding, roundabout route, so the letters take a new order
middle of tells us to take the centre letter of war

explanation.surface: An army cunningly redraws its forward positions around the heart of the battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviously' rearranges RESHAPED into SPERHEAD, and 'round' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearhead is the leading force of an attack, the front line of an advance.

clue.text: Colour of little wound?

parts.note: a scar is the mark a wound leaves
-let is a suffix meaning little, as in piglet or booklet

explanation.surface: A question about what shade a minor cut turns.
explanation.walkthrough: The suffix comes second: 'little wound' is a diminutive of the wound word, as booklet is a little book.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant red, one particular colour.

clue.text: Small guitar strummer without large range

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: without tells us the letter for large is removed from the strummer word

parts.note: a plectrum is the pick a guitarist strums with
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A guitarist with a small pick, lacking a large one, apparently has some range.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full range or scale of something, from one extreme to the other.

clue.text: Fix time for drink

parts.note: to pin something is to fix it in place
T is the abbreviation for time, as in physics formulae

explanation.surface: Arranging a time to meet for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is a standard measure of beer served in British pubs, so a drink.

clue.text: Fast one from con man on the phone

indicators.note: on the phone signals a word heard rather than seen, as a voice is over a telephone line

parts.note: a cheater is a swindler or con man

explanation.surface: A swindler pulls a quick trick during a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast one' suggests a con, as in 'pull a fast one', but it means a speedy animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, so a fast one.

clue.text: Speed getting left behind animal

indicators.note: behind means the left letter is placed after the speed word

parts.note: rate means speed, as in rate of travel

explanation.surface: A fast creature leaving a slower one trailing in its wake.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratel is the honey badger, a fierce African and Asian animal.

clue.text: Second time around Queen soften

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second, as in 'wait a mo'

indicators.note: around means the date word surrounds the Queen letters

parts.note: a date is a fixed time
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: On a second attempt, the Queen is asked to tone things down.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate is to make less extreme or harsh, which is to soften.

clue.text: Some singers are poetic backing musical works

indicators.note: backing means the hidden run is read in reverse, from right to left
Some indicates that only part of the letters in singers are poetic is taken

explanation.surface: A remark that certain vocalists are rather lyrical in support of musical pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Operas are dramatic compositions set to music, a standard kind of musical work.

clue.text: Actually taking on phone company owing money

indicators.note: taking on means the word for actually absorbs the phone company letters inside it

parts.note: indeed means actually or in fact
BT is British Telecom, the UK's main telephone company

explanation.surface: Someone is in fact signing up with a telecoms firm and running up a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indebted means being in debt, so owing money to a lender.

clue.text: Mass said first for puritan

parts.note: M is the physics abbreviation for mass
oral means spoken or said aloud rather than written
1ST, with the digit 1 read as the letter I, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: A Catholic Mass recited at the start of the day suits a strict religious person.
explanation.definitionFit: A puritan is someone with strict moral views who judges others, which is what a moralist is.

clue.text: Nice bust remodelled on French article

indicators.note: on means the article follows the rearranged letters in a down answer
remodelled means the letters of bust are reshaped into another order

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A sculptor recasts an attractive bust of a French subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' could be the French city; here it means fine or precise, as in a nice distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice can mean fine or delicate in distinction, as in a nice point, which is subtle.

clue.text: Starting to appear less exciting really, initially

definitions.text: Starting to appear less exciting really, initially

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Something that was once thrilling is beginning to seem duller.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the initial letters spell the answer, and the clue as a whole describes something beginning to look less fresh and exciting.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale means no longer fresh or interesting, so the comparative describes something growing duller.

clue.text: Bar in club is trouble

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of letters club is trouble

explanation.surface: A rowdy drinking establishment inside a nightclub is causing problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small restaurant or bar serving drinks and simple meals.

clue.text: Ailment's best treated ringing hospital foundation

indicators.note: ringing means the rearranged letters surround the hospital letter
treated suggests the letters are worked on and rearranged, like a condition being treated

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An illness is best dealt with by phoning the hospital, says a medical charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges AILMENTSBEST into ESTABLISMENT, and 'ringing' puts H inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: An establishment is an institution set up for a purpose, as is a foundation such as a charity or college.

clue.text: Devouring extract of ginseng or ginger

indicators.note: extract of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone gobbling down an extract of herbal roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Engorging means gorging, eating greedily, which is devouring food.

clue.text: Alleged drunk swallowing very big measure

indicators.note: swallowing means the drink word takes the size letters inside it

parts.note: supped means drank or drunk, as in sipped a liquid
OS is outsize, a clothing measure for very large garments

explanation.surface: A man said to be drunk after downing a huge measure of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as intoxicated, but it is the past of drink, sipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed means claimed or assumed to be so without proof, as is alleged.

clue.text: Children go nuts almost shaking teddy?

indicators.note: shaking means the letters are jumbled into a new order
almost means the last letter of nuts is dropped

explanation.surface: Kids going wild and nearly shaking their teddy bear to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teddy' looks like a toy bear, but it is also a one-piece undergarment for women; the question mark flags the example. 'almost' trims nuts to NUT before 'shaking' mixes it with CHILDRENGO.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy is a woman's one-piece undergarment, an example of underwear, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Published piece that shows where one stands

parts.note: ran means published, as a newspaper ran a story
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A newspaper article that reveals a person's position on an issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is a position in a list or table, showing someone's standing relative to others.

clue.text: Stuck, the compiler's turned white

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves, so the compiler's becomes I'M, 'I am'
paled means grew pale, turned white

explanation.surface: The crossword setter admits to going pale with fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaled means pierced through with something sharp, so stuck as on a spike.

clue.text: Loud instruments and quiet instruments?

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
lutes are stringed instruments

explanation.surface: An orchestra contrasts its noisy and gentle instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: these woodwinds are among the quieter instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Flutes are soft-toned woodwinds, one example of gentle-sounding instruments.

clue.text: Greek god's about gutted accepting heathens

indicators.note: about means the god's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild, and the 's gives PANS

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters of accepting

explanation.surface: A Greek deity is devastated at having to welcome unbelievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like the god's emotion, but it empties accepting to its ends, AG.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagans are people outside the main world religions, which heathens also are.

clue.text: Porridge in heartless gaol, full of regret

indicators.note: full of means the outer gaol letters are stuffed with the regret word
heartless means the middle letters of gaol are removed, leaving its outside

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A remorseful prisoner eats the cold porridge served in a cruel jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' is also British slang for a prison sentence, which the gaol imagery plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruel is thin porridge made by boiling oats in water or milk.

clue.text: Physical work's rejected in pen

indicators.note: in puts the turned work letters inside the pen word

parts.note: a corral is a pen or enclosure for livestock

indicators.note: rejected means the work abbreviation is turned back to front

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A sculptor's bodily piece is turned down and locked in an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal means relating to the body, as in corporal punishment, so it is a synonym of physical.

clue.text: Reportedly wriggled out of tube

indicators.note: Reportedly means we hear a word as spoken rather than see it written

parts.note: ducked means dodged or wriggled out of, as in ducked a question

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have squirmed their way out of a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A duct is a channel or pipe carrying air or fluid, so a tube.

clue.text: Boss promises to pay hard-working

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a round knob projecting from a surface
an IOU ('I owe you') is a written promise to pay a debt; IOUS is the plural

explanation.surface: An employer hands out promissory notes to a diligent worker instead of wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests an employer, but here it is a decorative knob or stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Studious describes someone diligent and devoted to study, so hard-working in an academic sense.

clue.text: Mournful song from Led Zeppelin singer penning single

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the singer's name surrounds the letter for single

parts.note: Robert Plant was the lead vocalist of the rock band Led Zeppelin
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for single

explanation.surface: A rock vocalist writes a sad song to be released as a single record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' and 'single' suggest writing a hit record, but they mean enclosing the numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaint is a lament or complaint, often expressed in poetry or song, so a mournful song.

clue.text: Silver brought back covered by excise charge

indicators.note: covered by means the turned silver letters sit inside the excise word

parts.note: to excise is to cut out or delete

indicators.note: brought back means the silver symbol is turned round

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Smuggled silver is liable to a customs duty when brought back into the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excise' and 'charge' look like customs duties; here excise is a verb meaning cut out, and charge means to entrust someone with a task.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate is to charge or entrust another person with a task or responsibility.

clue.text: Declines to go after circular saws

indicators.note: to go after means the decline word is placed after the circular word

parts.note: a circular is an advertising leaflet, an ad
ages, as a verb, means grows older and declines

explanation.surface: Someone turns down the job of using a circular saw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saws' looks like cutting tools after 'circular', but it is the noun for old sayings.
explanation.definitionFit: Saws are traditional sayings or proverbs, just as adages are.
